description:
Dispatcher for note operations: create, render, edit, query.

Subcommands:
  new — create a new note and open it for editing (interactive)
  copy [FILTER] — pick a note, copy contents to a new timestamped note (interactive)
  strip [FILTER] — pick a note, copy contents without the body, for templating (interactive)
  edit [FILTER] — pick a note, open in the default editor (interactive)
  nano [FILTER] — pick a note, open in nano (interactive)
  last — open the most recently-created note; the only non-interactive subcommand
  delete [FILTER] — pick a note and permanently delete it (interactive)
  cat [FILTER] — pick a note and print it to stdout (interactive)
  pdf [FILTER] — pick a note, render PDF plus markdown with an ACTION/TASK summary (interactive)
  minutes [FILTER] — pick a note, render meeting minutes: TOC plus AGREED/RESOLVED/ACTION summary (interactive)
  agenda [FILTER] — pick a note, render a meeting agenda (interactive)

Args:
  SUBCOMMAND — optional; with none, runs `new`.
  FILTER — optional case-insensitive substring narrowing the picker list.

Examples:
  ["last"]

Notes:
  Call only `last`. Every other subcommand — including the no-argument default `new` — opens an interactive picker and reads a selection from stdin; with no terminal it consumes EOF and behaves unpredictably rather than erroring.
  To find or read notes non-interactively use `search notes` for pointers and a file reader for bodies. To capture content non-interactively use `buffer add-text` / `buffer add-action`.
  `delete` permanently removes the file.
  Rendering subcommands write into the export directory (default the user's Downloads folder) and need pandoc plus a LaTeX engine.
  Body keywords a note may carry: ACTION: (ingested by `tasks`), TASK: (already ingested; never write by hand), AGREED:, RESOLVED:, !: .

BLOCKED: new, copy, strip, edit, nano, last, delete, cat, pdf, minutes, agenda. These subcommands are refused and calling one returns an error. Do not attempt them.
